site.name: Itqan
site.strapline: Know where you stand. See the shortest path to the job you want.
site.description: Itqan shows you where you stand today, which role to aim for, and the shortest path there. Real jobs and real courses matched to your position. In Arabic and English.

chat.title: Hud
chat.limit: Answers about Itqan. Anything about your own record needs an account.
chat.greeting: Hello. I am Hud. Ask me about Itqan: what it does, what it does not do, and what happens to your documents.
chat.noMatchBody: I do not have a ready answer for that. I can answer questions about Itqan itself: what it does, what it costs, and what happens to your documents. Anything about you specifically I cannot answer until I have read what you give me, and that starts with a free account.

forks.keywords: what does do how work works working product itqan
forks.a: You give it whatever you already have. It reads that, tells you where you stand today, and helps you settle on the role to aim for. Then it shows the shortest path there in real courses, and the live openings you can apply to now, each with the reason it fits.

forks.keywords: free cost costs price pay paid payment money subscription plan card charge trial
forks.a: We offer different plans to fit different needs. The core is free: the gap, the full path, your job matches and the advisor. A premium tier covers extended use of the AI, and nobody pays to get hired.

forks.keywords: transcript document documents upload privacy data record certificate store stored delete safe security
forks.a: They get read so Itqan can work out where you stand. Before anything moves on from there, everything it read is put in front of you to check and correct. That screen is where the decision sits, and it is yours rather than ours.

forks.q: My degree is not from Oman. Does that work?
forks.keywords: outside oman abroad foreign international degree university visa sponsor gulf english expat
forks.a: Yes. Itqan is built for Arabic and English equally, and it reads qualifications from outside the Gulf. Where it is unsure it says so and asks you to confirm, rather than guessing.

problem.heading: It is not you. It is the guessing.

cards.title: A hundred applications, no answers
cards.body: You apply, you wait, you hear nothing. Most of those roles were never a fit, and you find that out after the evening is gone.

cards.title: Every posting looks close enough
cards.body: The title fits. One line in the requirements does not. So you apply on a guess, or you close the tab on a guess.

cards.title: Nobody tells you what to fix
cards.body: You know roughly where you want to end up. No one has shown you the distance, or what to close first.

items.a: The parts that get you into work are free and stay free: where you stand, your path, your job matches and the advisor. A premium tier covers extended use of the AI. Nothing you need is behind it.

items.q: What do you need from me?
items.a: Whatever you already have. A CV, certificates, an academic record. Then a few short questions so Itqan knows what you are aiming for. The more it has, the sharper the fit.

items.q: Do you find real jobs, or just give advice?
items.a: Real openings that exist right now, matched to your position and your preferences, each with the reason it fits. Itqan does not promise you a job. It shows you where you have a real chance and where you do not.

items.q: What if I do not know what job I want?
items.a: That is the common case, and it is the first thing Itqan works on. It reads what you have and suggests roles your position already supports, so you are choosing between real options instead of guessing.

items.q: Where do the recommendations come from?
items.a: Openings and courses that exist, read against what those jobs currently ask for. Not a generic checklist of what a role is supposed to need.
Yes, at any time. Deleting your account removes everything you gave Itqan and everything built from it.

hiw.title: How Itqan works
hiw.metaDescription: Four steps from what you already have to the shortest path to the job you want. No inflated numbers, no promises.
hiw.intro: Four steps. No magic in any of them.

steps.title: You bring what you already have
steps.body: A CV, certificates, an academic record. Whatever exists. Not a form with twenty fields.

steps.title: Itqan tells you where you stand
steps.body: It shows you everything it read, exactly as it read it, and you correct anything wrong. Nothing moves forward until you approve it. A position you checked yourself is worth more than one you were handed.

steps.title: You choose the role to aim for
steps.body: If you know it, say it. If you do not, Itqan suggests roles your position already supports and you pick from real options.

steps.title: You get the path and the jobs
steps.body: The courses and certifications that close the distance, in order, and the openings you can apply to today. Each one carries its reason and a source you can open.

proof.title: Proof
proof.metaDescription: A full worked example of how Itqan judges where you stand against a real role, with its current limits stated plainly.
proof.heading: Do not take our word for it
proof.intro: This page shows the reasoning itself, so you can judge it before creating an account.

example.heading: One role, read against one person
example.intro: What a Junior Data Analyst opening asks for, and where this person stands on each one.

rows.why: Two of your database courses were built on writing queries and designing tables. That is what a posting means by SQL.
Your statistics work covers describing data, probability and reading results, which is the whole of what these postings ask for.
The monthly reporting on your CV is this, under a different name. The market calls it reporting.
Nothing you gave shows it, and three of the openings tracked for this role ask for it by name. That puts it first on your path.
Your technical writing course points at it but does not evidence it on its own, so it is a suggestion until you confirm it.

example.note: An illustrative example. Inside the product, each match links to a live posting with the date it was retrieved.

how.heading: How a recommendation is justified
how.p1: A recommendation is a chain with three links: where you stand, what the role asks for, and an opening that asks for it right now. Itqan shows the whole chain every time, under the name why this match.
how.p2: When every link holds, it says so. When one is weaker, it is labelled a suggestion for you to confirm. It is never presented as fact.

limits.heading: What Itqan cannot do yet
items: It cannot promise you a job. It shows you where you stand and what closes the distance. The applying is still yours.
It has not published an accuracy figure, because measurement on enough real cases is not finished. A number before that would be a guess.
Some results are suggestions to confirm, not facts. They are labelled.
What you upload is a starting point, not the whole picture of you. Projects, work and character live outside it.
It reads Arabic and English. Other languages, not yet.

privacy.title: Privacy

privacy.heading: How your data is handled
privacy.noticeLabel: A lawyer completes this section. Questions to answer:

sections.heading: What is collected
questions: Which fields are required at sign up?
Are the original files kept, or only the extracted text?
What usage data or technical logs are collected?

sections.heading: Why it is collected
questions: What is the lawful basis for each processing purpose? Explicit consent is the only basis available.
Is data used to improve the models? If so, under what consent?

sections.heading: How long it is kept
questions: How long is an inactive account kept?
When are uploaded files permanently deleted?

sections.heading: Who it is shared with
questions: Who are the hosting and processing providers, and where are their servers?
Does data leave Oman, and under what safeguards?

sections.heading: Your rights
questions: How does a user request a copy of their data?
How is consent withdrawn, and what happens after withdrawal?
What is the response time for requests?

sections.heading: Contact the data officer
questions: Who is the data protection officer?
What is the official email and postal address?

about.title: Who we are
about.metaDescription: Why we built Itqan. We show you where you stand, the shortest path to the job you want, and the real jobs that fit you today.
about.whyHeading: You know roughly where you want to end up. Nobody tells you how far that is, or which way to go.
about.whyBody: We built Itqan because that distance should be visible from the start, not discovered after a year of applying and hearing nothing. The hard part was never what you already have. It is knowing what stands between you and where you want to be, and what to do about it first.
about.mission: We show you where you stand, the shortest path to the job you want, and the real jobs that fit you today.
about.vision: A world where nobody has to guess their next step.
about.how1Title: We measure against the real market.
about.how1Body: Live Gulf demand and what those openings currently ask for, not a generic checklist of what a role is supposed to need.
about.how2Body: Every recommendation carries its reason and a real source you can open. Nothing invented is ever shown to you.
about.how3Body: No employer can buy a place in what you see.
about.what1Body: today, against the role you want.
about.what2Body: across the distance, in real courses.
about.what3Title: Brings the jobs that fit you now,
about.evidenceHeading: We asked graduates and final year students in Oman.
about.evidenceBody: Roughly two thirds had read a job posting and could not tell whether something they had done counted as the skill being asked for. Nearly nine in ten were blocked by postings demanding experience they did not have. Nearly half of those who were rejected could not say why.
about.evidenceQualifier: An early sample, drawn from the graduates we are launching to. We are widening it.
about.whereBody: We are embedded at UTAS, which is both our first pilot and where our survey came from. Our regulator, MTCIT, runs Khuta, which we treat as a distribution channel rather than a competitor. We start in Oman, then Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf.
about.payEyebrow: What you will never pay for
about.payBody: You never pay for the parts that get you into work. Where you stand, your path, your job matches and the advisor are free and stay free. A premium tier covers extended use of the AI, never the parts that get you hired. Employers and universities pay for access to candidates who agreed to it.
about.refuse1: We will not sell a place in your results.
about.refuse2: We will not invent a course or a job that does not exist.
about.refuse3: We will not promise you a job.
about.refuse4: We will not publish an accuracy figure we have not measured.
